title: The Hanging Sun
lens: Interlocking loops around a landmark (Super Metroid's Brinstar, Metroid Dread, Dark Souls' Firelink web, folded into 2D)
pitch: The wood is a bowl with one thing in the middle: a dead oak with the firefly's biggest lamp, the Hanging Sun, slung in its crown inside a great orb web. The last stragglers of the swarm circle it because they think it is the moon. Every room draws it at its true bearing, so it is the compass: left of it, right of it, under it, and at last above it. Three lanterns hang on the web's frame, one west, one east and one on top, and each one is reached only by going all the way round the oak by a different loop: down the west slope and back up through the roots, under the clearing through the drowned roots and up the Moon Well, and over the top along the Skein. Every loop comes out somewhere you've already been, from a side you never saw: the glade where you got your wings, the bolted door in your own hub, your own empty cocoon. Each lantern you put out cuts a frame line, so the web sags and the Sun dims and tilts as seen from every room. The landmark is the progress bar and the to-do list, with no signposts. The great dragonfly you've watched cross the Sun all game is the boss. You fight it in the Sun's swinging light, cut the Sun down, and it falls straight down the hollow oak into the hub where you've been resting, and the real moon shines down the trunk for the first time.
throughline: Wing wants the stragglers back, and they are circling the Hanging Sun because they think it is the moon, so she has to get round it to every side and put it out.

regions.name: The Hatching Bough
regions.note: The cocoon row on a high bough. The swarm streams east along the Long Limb into the Sun's glow. Tatter's hop fails at the promise gap, and the bough's tip snaps under her. Revisit (19:30, from the Long Limb): her empty cocoon becomes the moon patch for the boss, and Tatter crosses the fallen root. With claws: a firefly sign on the cocoon row's top.

regions.name: The Rimfall
regions.note: A downhill chase along the rim's fallen trunk after three stragglers, with two real drops. The vista at the lip shows the whole bowl in one frame: the Sun and its three lanterns, the web, the Skein's twigs against the sky, the Long Limb, the roots' black mouth, the Moon Well's beam far east. The title shows over the moon while she runs. Dense: stragglers to chase, a wick in the trunk hollow (a find), leaves to hack.

regions.name: The Leaning Wood
regions.note: The first flames, under leaning pines. One flame over a gap is the first fling, then a two-flame chain. Juveniles eat dead moths in a wick's pool: fight them or fling over. There are leaf curtains to hack, and one curtain that never sways (the moth-stone). A claws lock: a kick-face up the leaning pine to a high wick.

regions.name: The Drying Pine
regions.note: A hollow in the leaning pine, with real moonlight through a split: glide. A dark knot-hole sits high in the back wall, with no way up. The lip opens east over the Web Wall. Revisit (8:00): she comes OUT of that knot-hole from the chimney and looks down on the spot where she basked. The bark plug falls, and the knot-hole's branch runs east to the Crook.

regions.name: The Web Wall
regions.note: The bowl's west floor, up against the Sun's web: silk from the floor to the crown, the Sun burning behind it, moths stuck in it. Danglers drop from the oak's low limbs onto the cut spots under two wicks. Hawkers dive at the moths through gaps in the web. Touching the silk calls its weaver. The beetles' burrow floor (pogo) is the way down. After the West Lantern: the web's skirt lifts off the floor and the trunk's shadow niche opens, and beetles come up to eat the fallen.

regions.name: The Sinkroots
regions.note: Dark root halls under the Web Wall. The only light is where dead moths fall through cracks, and beetles feed in those pools. A crust shelf breaks under a pogo. The east end is the hub's west door, and the west end climbs into the chimney. Quiet between the pools: contrast before the climb.

regions.name: The Glowcap Chimney
regions.note: A black shaft that the firefly lit with a ladder of glow-caps: a vertical fling chain, a dangler on each rest ledge, and a ceiling it seems to end at. Embers relight on a fall, so a retry takes seconds. It ends at a bark plug, which is the Drying Pine's knot-hole.

regions.name: The Pine Crook
regions.note: A pine limb reaching for the Sun, level with the West Lantern. A fling chain runs over the web's outer silk (touch it and the weaver runs out), with a hawker on the orbit. The lantern takes two hits or a fling through, and its frame line parts: a cloud lifts past the moon, the web's west half sags, and the Sun tilts and dims, seen from everywhere. The Orbit (optional) starts here.

regions.name: The Undersun
regions.note: The hub: a hollow in the root plate directly under the oak. A moon patch, silence, a black pool, and wings drifting down through the crack in the ceiling where the Sun glows. Three ways: the west door (Sinkroots), the pool's root ledges down (Drowned Roots), and the east gate, root-bolted from the far side. The pool's west shallows breathe (the midden). Both early loops start and end here, in either order, and the Sun falls into it.

regions.name: The Drowned Roots
regions.note: Root arches over black water where the dead moths float. Glide gaps run from arch to arch. Backswimmers strike up through the surface at whatever lands near them, with a ring of ripples first. Danglers hang over the dry landings, one wick to a pocket. A warm reflection with no source (the cold lantern). The far end glows silver: the Moon Well. The Sun is out of sight here, the only place it is.

regions.name: The Moon Well
regions.note: A sinkhole open to the sky, the one place on the bowl's floor the real moon reaches. Claws, in the pool of moonlight at its foot. Its walls are the claws' first climb: two faces and a rest ledge with a wick. From its lip she looks west across the Thornbank at the Sun, and the stub east to the valley lies beyond.

regions.name: The Thornbank
regions.note: The east floor: a thorn thicket climbing toward the East Lantern. The Sun is on her LEFT now, and through the web she sees her own Web Wall. Hawkers hunt the orbit, and a beetle guards the spire's foot. Thorn bands to pogo across, and a fling chain up the spire to the lantern. The root-bolted gate in its floor is the hub's east door. Revisit: the hawkers from dead lanterns gather here.

regions.name: The Mossback
regions.note: A mossy dead trunk on the east rim, climbed with claws: kick-faces, rest ledges with wicks, a hawker crossing the faces, a dangler at the top. A kick-glide off its east face reaches the Crow's Eye (secret).

regions.name: The Skein
regions.note: The highest canopy: thin twigs and silk bridges over the crown. The Sun is below her for the first time, with the stragglers orbiting under her feet and the dragonfly passing beneath. Hawkers patrol the gaps, with wicks to fling between. The Crown Lantern below is snuffed by dropping onto its flames and pogoing down them. Then the web collapses onto the Sun. Its west end drops onto the Long Limb.

regions.name: The Long Limb
regions.note: The swarm's road from minute 0: a fallen limb from the hatch to the oak's crown, crusted with husks of stuck moths, with danglers under it. The slack web at its east tip is the boss door. At its west end are the promise gap and the hanging root.

regions.name: The Sun's Cradle
regions.note: The boss arena: the oak's open crown around the Hanging Sun, a cage of glow-caps and lanterns on one chain. The ruined web hangs below like a net. The Long Limb's tip is to the west and the Mossback's face across the gap to the east. The Emperor's orbit fills it.

landmarks.name: The Hanging Sun (and the dragonfly crossing it)
The Undersun's crack (the Sun's glow from below)

secrets.name: The moth-stone (the area's map; none before it)
secrets.tell: One leaf curtain in the Leaning Wood hangs still while every other one sways: it is backed by stone. Hack it.

secrets.name: The Wing Midden: the old burrback, optional mini-boss, a moon-drop (+1 health)
secrets.tell: The Undersun pool's west shallows are a curved grey 'rock' that rises and falls if she stands still. Three pogos break the crust and the rock wakes up.

secrets.name: The trunk's shadow (firefly sign 1)
secrets.tell: When the West Lantern goes, the web's skirt lifts off the Web Wall's floor. In the oak's shadow there is one dark gap where no light falls.

secrets.name: The cold lantern (10 moths, firefly sign 2)
secrets.tell: A warm smear on the Drowned Roots' black water with no lamp above it. It is a reflection from behind a root curtain.

secrets.name: The Crow's Eye (moonlit hollow: long breath)
secrets.tell: From the Skein, looking east, one 'star' sits too low among the trees. It is moonlight through a hole in the Mossback, reached by a kick-glide off its far face.

secrets.name: The Orbit (optional challenge: sharp wings, 60 moths)
secrets.tell: From the Crook, a ring of tiny flames is plainly visible round the outside of the web, like a rosary. The way round is the hard part, not the finding.

secrets.name: The cocoon row's top (firefly sign 3)
secrets.tell: At the boss's moon patch, one unhatched cocoon higher up glows faintly warm. Claws up the trunk.

boss.name: The Emperor (the dragonfly that hunts the Sun's orbit)
boss.idea: Not a spider. A great dusk dragonfly that has crossed the Sun as a silhouette in every room all game, eating stragglers off the orbit. P1, the orbit (~45 s): it circles the Sun on a wide readable ellipse, breaks off to dive at her (a silver wing-flare, a hover, a hum), and stalls after the dive. The Sun's cage flames ring the arena as fling points, and a fling into its path with a cut in the launch knocks it out of orbit for a punish window (the Crook's lesson). P2, the swing (~45 s): stunned, it crashes into the chain and the Sun swings. Now it hunts only what the swinging light touches, so she rides the moving shadow on the Long Limb's tip and the Mossback's face with claws, and cuts it when it overshoots into the dark. This is the pillar 'the dark is safe' as a boss mechanic (the Thornbank's and Mossback's lessons). P3, the fall (~40 s): wings torn, it clings to the swinging Sun itself. She pogoes on its back and on the cage flames (the Skein's drop-and-pogo) and then cuts the last link. The Sun falls with it down the hollow oak. Weaver-easy as a first boss: one tell to learn each phase, the whole arena on screen, her cocoon 20 s away.

minuteByMinute: 0–1: the cocoon, the swarm leaving along the Long Limb toward a warm light that isn't the moon, Tatter's failed hop, the bough snapping. Control in seconds.
1–2: the Rimfall chase and the vista: the whole bowl is the map, the Sun its centre, the three lanterns its to-do list, the dragonfly crossing it. The title shows while she runs.
2–3: the Leaning Wood: the first fling, a two-flame chain, juveniles feeding at a wick's pool, one leaf curtain that doesn't sway.
3–5: the Drying Pine (glide, a knot-hole she can't reach), the glide out to the Web Wall: silk floor to crown, danglers, hawkers, the West Lantern out of reach overhead; the burrow floor gives way.
5–6: the Undersun. Silence, a moon patch, the Sun's glow through the crack, a bolted east gate, a black pool. Two ways, and the player picks (the run goes west).
6–8: the Sinkroots in the dark, then the Glowcap Chimney: a vertical fling ladder with embers on a fall.
8–10: out of the knot-hole above her own glade ('oh'), along the Crook, a chain over the web's silk, the West Lantern out. Seen from anywhere, the Sun now sags to the west.
10–11: the glide down, the trunk's shadow niche for the curious, back to the Undersun, rest.
11–13: the Drowned Roots: the only stretch with no Sun in sight, black water, backswimmers' ripples, glide gaps, a silver light ahead. The Moon Well: claws in real moonlight.
13–16: up the well; the Thornbank with the Sun on the wrong side and her Web Wall across the silk; the thorn spire; the East Lantern out; the root bolt is her hub's east gate ('oh'). Rest.
16–19: up the Mossback with claws, onto the Skein: looking down on the Sun, the orbit under her feet; the drop-and-pogo down the Crown Lantern; the web collapses.
19–21: dropped onto the Long Limb, she walks west to the promise gap and finds her own cocoon ('oh'). The root bridge, Tatter crosses, the moon patch. East along the swarm's road to the crown.
21–24: the Emperor: orbit, swing, fall. The last link.

24–25: the Sun falls down the hollow oak into the Undersun's pool and goes out with a hiss. The moon comes straight down the trunk onto the hub: Gust. Every moth she freed rises up the trunk past the real moon. The way on is east, past the Moon Well.
